chapter: Recordings as a leader and the Getz years
title: Autumn in New York and Scratch with Holland and Humair
summary: Uptown trio record, then Enja's Scratch, a first-meeting session that won a Paris award.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: The next one, 1985, is one you already referenced, the Autumn in New York, with Rufus Reid and Freddie. It’s Uptown Records. Then Scratch, Dave Holland and Daniel Humair, Enja Records. That must have been done – no, you could do them here and then just lease them to those guys over there.
Yeah, but that one was for Enja.

For Enja. No, that one wasn’t leased. That was their – that was the company. That was their suggestion, to do that. I had never met Dave or Daniel before the studio. So there was no rehearsal or anything with that. I brought some music, and Dave had a tune. That’s basically it. We just played. It was interesting, because it made me play differently, playing with those two guys. It brought out a different thing for me. That record actually won, in Paris, an award. So yeah, that was definitely a lot of fun to do.
